title: Codex Desktop continuously generates Crashpad pending dumps, growing without any limit: +5GB per day at least
excerpt: Summary Codex Desktop is continuously adding paired .dmp and _sidecar.json files under: ~/Library/Application Support/com.openai.codex/web/Crashpad/pending On my machine this directory grew to 4.9G...
content_html:
6. changed the title

    [-]Codex Desktop continuously generates Crashpad pending dumps, growing to ~5GB[/-] [+]Codex Desktop continuously generates Crashpad pending dumps, growing without any limit: +5GB per day at least[/+]

    on Jun 9, 2026

  26. Still happening on the current build, and at a much larger scale. Measured 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-17:

    Environment

    • ChatGPT.app 26.1007.71326 (build 20398), Codex Framework (Chromium) 155.0.8059.40
    • macOS 15.7.4, Apple Silicon (arm64)

    What I found

    Folder Size Files
    ~/Library/Application Support/com.openai.codex/web/Crashpad 180 GB 2,251,765
    ~/Library/Application Support/Codex/Crashpad (almost all of it in pending/) 143 GB 1,785,095
    Total ~323 GB ~4.04 million

    That was about 35% of a 926 GB disk. Free space fell to 1.4 GB before I found it. Nothing in the app warned me. I only found it by running du over ~/Library.

    The app kept working the whole time, as others have reported here. So the dumps build up silently in the background with no limit.

    Cleanup

    With the app still running, I renamed both Crashpad folders and deleted the renamed copies. Free space went from 1.4 GB to 50+ GB within minutes, and the delete is still running (millions of small files).

    Asks

    1. Put a size or count cap on Crashpad/pending, with automatic pruning (see also Add storage limits and automatic cleanup for Codex-generated data #51361).
    2. Stop the handler crash loop that produces the dumps ([app][macOS][26.727.51351] browser_crashpad_handler SIGTRAPs 2ms after launch, launchd respawns it, Crashpad/pending fills disk at ~17GB/day #36982).
    3. Show a warning in the app when its own data goes over a few GB.

    Related: #36982, #39875, #51739, #52194, #51361.
